column4: The section's cushions and couches furnish a garden room; this verse places reconciled brothers on couches facing one another, إِخْوَانًا عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ, a direct social use of the same furniture.
The section treats the raised sky as the world's roof; this ayah says the nearest sky is adorned with stars, adding a specific decoration to that overhead scene.
Before 41:10 places mountains and apportions provision, this ayah says the earth was created in two days; it supplies the opening stage of the measured construction sequence.

This ayah pictures silver roofs over earthly houses, سَقْفًا مِّن فِضَّةٍ; the section's raised sky is a cosmic roof, while 43:35 calls such wealth worldly enjoyment, adding a temporal boundary to the furnished-world image.
This ayah adds doors and couches people recline upon in the same earthly houses; 43:35 frames that luxury as worldly enjoyment, a boundary alongside the section's garden couches.
After the couches of 52:20, this ayah has garden dwellers pass a cup among themselves, كَأْسًا; it shows how a cup in the section's room is used in company.
After the couches and facing guests of 56:15–16, this ayah names cups and pitchers from a flowing spring; it extends the furnished scene to the section's placed cups.
The section explicitly cites the balance placed with the raised sky in 55:7; this ayah again pairs the revealed balance with people establishing justice, الْمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ.
The section's sky-as-roof image receives a parallel adornment here: the nearest sky is decorated with lamps, مَصَابِيحَ, continuing the crafted-ceiling image.
Before 79:28 says the sky's height was raised and proportioned, this ayah asks whether human creation or the sky is harder and says He built it; it emphasizes the sky as a constructed work.

The section sets mountains in the earth and the sky above as canopy; here the mountain is lifted over a people like a shade, كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ, reversing the mountain's place in that room-and-world arrangement.
